constraints: Use DESeq2 with design ~condition; control must be the reference level

steps.name: edgeR QL cross-check and concordance
caveats: Different filtering between packages changes the tested-gene denominator; overlap must be computed on the intersection of tested genes
Spearman correlation of log2FC will be high even when significance calls disagree — high correlation is not evidence that the significance calls are robust
steps.context: At n=3 per group edgeR's quasi-likelihood F-test is generally more conservative than the DESeq2 Wald test, and limma-voom is more conservative still. Agreement across all three is the strongest statement this dataset can support about any individual gene; disagreement identifies genes whose call is an artefact of one dispersion model.
steps.question: Does an independent negative-binomial framework (edgeR quasi-likelihood) recover the same treated-vs-control genes as DESeq2, and where do the two disagree?
constraints: Use identical sample-to-condition assignment and identical contrast direction as T1S1
Apply each method's own recommended filtering; report how many genes each method tested so overlap counts are interpretable
Do not present the union of the three methods as the result — the union inflates the apparent gene count
If any method returns zero significant genes, report that plainly rather than switching to nominal p-values as the headline
steps.description: Re-run the same treated vs control contrast on the same counts.csv/metadata.csv with edgeR: filterByExpr, TMM normalisation, estimateDisp, glmQLFit and glmQLFTest on ~condition. Produce a concordance report: number of genes significant in each method at padj<0.05 and padj<0.1, the pairwise overlaps (with a Venn or UpSet figure), Spearman correlation of the log2FC estimates across all tested genes, and a rank-rank plot. acceptance_criteria: Significant gene counts from edgeR-QL and limma-voom are reported at the same thresholds used in T1S1

steps.name: Power and false-discovery audit for n=3
caveats: Post-hoc power computed from the same data that produced the effect estimates is descriptive of the design, not of the truth of any specific gene — do not compute per-gene post-hoc power for significant genes and present it as confirmation
With 6 samples the permutation null is extremely coarse and cannot certify a low FDR; it can only detect gross miscalibration
Full re-running of DESeq2 on 10 label configurations is cheap at this matrix size but must reuse identical filtering settings for the counts to be comparable
steps.context: The second half of the research question — how confident can we be with three replicates — is a quantitative claim that must be computed, not asserted. With 6 samples the number of distinct 3-vs-3 label splits is exactly C(6,3)/2 = 10, so the permutation null is enumerable in full rather than sampled, but it is also coarse: the minimum attainable permutation p-value is 1/10 = 0.1, which itself bounds how strong an empirical-null statement can be. Say that bound out loud rather than reporting a permutation p-value as if it were fine-grained.
steps.question: Given the dispersions actually observed in these 6 liver samples, what effect size is detectable at 80% power with 3 replicates per group, and how does the pipeline behave under permuted labels?
constraints: Estimate dispersions from this dataset — do not substitute a literature default BCV
Enumerate all distinct 3-vs-3 splits rather than random sampling, and state that the permutation null has a floor of p=0.1
Do not report the power analysis as if it validated the gene list; it bounds what the gene list can mean
If the observed split's discovery count is not clearly separated from the permuted splits, state that the DE signal is not distinguishable from label noise
steps.description: Quantify the statistical confidence the design can support, using the dispersions estimated from this dataset rather than generic assumptions. (a) Summarise the DESeq2/edgeR dispersion distribution: median and quartiles of the biological coefficient of variation, overall and stratified by expression decile. (b) Compute, per expression stratum, the minimum detectable fold change at 80% power with n=3 per group at alpha corresponding to BH control over the ~12,000 tested genes — either analytically from the NB power formula or by parametric simulation from the fitted mean-dispersion relationship; state which was used. (c) Report what fraction of the 12,000 genes are so low-count or so overdispersed that no fold change below 4x is detectable. (d) Run a label-permutation experiment: for each of the possible non-trivial 3-vs-3 relabellings (there are 10 distinct splits, of which 9 are permuted), re-run the DESeq2 contrast and record the number of genes passing padj<0.05 and padj<0.1. Compare the true split against the permuted splits and report the empirical rank of the observed discovery count. (e) Report the observed-vs-expected p-value calibration (QQ plot, genomic-inflation-style lambda) for the true labels. Output a plain-language confidence verdict tying these numbers to the research question.
acceptance_criteria: Observed dispersion / BCV distribution is reported numerically, overall and by expression stratum
A minimum-detectable-fold-change curve or table at 80% power for n=3 per group is produced, with the method (analytic or simulation) named
The number of genes for which no fold change under 4x is detectable is reported
All 9 permuted 3-vs-3 label splits are run and their discovery counts tabulated against the true split, with the 1/10 resolution limit of this null stated explicitly
A written confidence verdict addresses the research question directly, without hedging into vagueness

steps.name: Ranked GSEA on hallmark and GO
caveats: The 12,000-gene matrix is a filtered universe, so gene-set background is not the full transcriptome and enrichment p-values are conditional on that filtering — state it
GSEA on an underpowered contrast can produce confident-looking NES values driven by a handful of genes; always inspect leading-edge size
If the human hallmark or GO sets are absent at run time, report the enrichment step as not run and carry the DE result forward unchanged — the research question survives without it
steps.context: Human liver tissue under drug treatment. Human hallmark (50 sets) and human GO BP/CC/MF gene sets are staged in the reference store as HGNC-symbol GMTs; the step must resolve them from the environment rather than a hardcoded path. Ranked GSEA is preferred over ORA here because with n=3 the thresholded significant list may be too short for a meaningful over-representation test, while a ranking retains information from sub-threshold coordinated shifts.
steps.question: Which hallmark and GO processes are coordinately shifted in drug-treated versus control human liver, including the xenobiotic-metabolism and stress-response programmes expected of a hepatic drug exposure?
constraints: Use HUMAN gene sets — the data is Homo sapiens; using mouse sets would silently produce meaningless results
Resolve the gene-set files from the environment's reference store by what they are (human hallmark, human GO), not by an assumed path
Use the full ranked gene list, not a thresholded subset, for fgsea
Report enrichment as coordinated expression shift, never as evidence of pathway activation or of drug mechanism
steps.description: Rank all tested genes by the DESeq2 shrunken log2FC (or by -log10(p) signed by fold-change direction; state which was used and why) and run fgsea against human hallmark gene sets and human GO Biological Process sets. Gene identifiers in counts.csv are already gene symbols (HGNC), matching the GMT identifier space directly — report the fraction of ranked genes that map to at least one set, since 12,000 genes is a pre-filtered universe. Regardless of significance, explicitly report the enrichment statistic and FDR for the liver-drug-relevant sets present in the collections — xenobiotic metabolism, bile acid metabolism, fatty acid metabolism, reactive oxygen species / oxidative stress, inflammatory and TNFA/NFKB response, apoptosis, and p53 — so their absence of change is as visible as their presence. The gene-symbol-to-gene-set mapping rate is reported
The named liver-drug-relevant sets are reported with their statistics whether or not they pass FDR
If ORA was skipped, the reason (significant list under 15 genes) is stated
GO BP results are collapsed for parent-child redundancy before any set count is reported

steps.name: Integrated DE report with confidence bounds
caveats: The temptation at n=3 is to loosen thresholds until a story appears; the report must resist this and state the underpowered case plainly if that is what the data show
Cross-method agreement reduces method-specific artefacts but does not protect against a shared confounder such as an unrecorded batch or a single outlier sample driving the contrast
steps.context: This is the deliverable that answers both halves of the research question in one place. It must not upgrade the certainty of any upstream step. If the analysis found few or no genes, the report says that and quantifies why, which is a complete and useful answer.
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which genes changed with drug treatment in liver', and what is the honest confidence statement for a 3-vs-3 unpaired design?
constraints: Do not describe any gene as a biomarker, target, or mechanism — no such evidence exists in this dataset

Do not present nominal p-values as the primary result if padj-significant genes are few; if nominal results are shown, label them as hypothesis-generating and give the expected false-positive count at that threshold
Every quantitative claim must trace to an upstream step's output
Use the actual condition labels from metadata.csv throughout
steps.description: Assemble a single report. Section 1: the design as profiled — 6 human liver samples, 3 drug-treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch, 12,000 genes from Salmon. Section 2: QC verdict from T1S1 (group separation on PCA, outliers, p-value calibration). Section 3: the gene list, presented as a tiered table — high-confidence (significant in DESeq2, edgeR-QL and limma-voom), tentative (significant in one or two), and the full ranked table as a supplement; give effect sizes with lfcSE, not just p-values. Section 4: the confidence answer from T2S1 — observed BCV, minimum detectable fold change at 80% power, the fraction of the transcriptome effectively untestable at this n, and the permutation comparison with its 1/10 resolution floor stated. Section 5: pathway-level context from T3S1, labelled as coordinated expression shift and not mechanism. Section 6: explicit limitations — what this design cannot establish (no dose, no time course, no drug identity in the profiled metadata, no paired structure, no independent replication cohort), and a concrete recommendation for the replicate count that would be needed to detect the fold-change range actually observed here. acceptance_criteria: The report states the number of high-confidence genes (all three methods) explicitly, including zero if that is the result
Effect sizes with standard errors accompany every gene called out by name
The confidence section gives numbers (BCV, minimum detectable fold change, untestable fraction) rather than adjectives
A replicate-count recommendation grounded in the observed dispersion is given
Limitations section names the absence of dose, time-course, drug identity and validation cohort

plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DE with n=3 power audit
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq experiment: raw Salmon gene-level counts for 12,000 genes across 6 human liver samples (counts.csv, 12000 x 7 with gene symbol as first column), and metadata.csv (6 x 2) giving one condition label per sample — 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired. The research question has two halves, and they are planned separately because they need different evidence.

Half one is the contrast itself. With n=3 per group and a single covariate, the correct estimator is a negative-binomial GLM with empirical-Bayes dispersion shrinkage — DESeq2 with a Wald test on ~condition — because at n=3 per-gene dispersion is essentially unestimable and the shared prior is doing most of the work. T1S1 does library-size normalisation, independent filtering, PCA/sample-distance QC (which must be inspected before the DE result is trusted: with three replicates one outlier sample can create or destroy the entire gene list), and the DESeq2 Wald contrast treated vs control with lfcShrink for ranking. T1S2 re-runs the same contrast with edgeR quasi-likelihood (glmQLFTest), which is the more conservative estimator at very small n, and reports the overlap. Concordance between two independent NB frameworks is the cheapest available guard against a method-specific artefact; discordance is itself a reportable finding.

Half two — 'how confident can we be with three replicates' — is not answerable by an adjective, so it gets its own quantitative track. T2S1 estimates the achieved power of this design directly from the fitted dispersions: the observed dispersion distribution, the fold change detectable at 80% power per expression stratum, the count of genes for which no realistic effect size is detectable, and a permutation/label-reshuffle null giving the empirical false-discovery behaviour of the pipeline on this exact matrix. That step is what licenses or refuses the confidence claim.

T3S1 puts the ranked list into biology with hallmark and GO gene sets (human, staged under /mnt/refs) using fgsea on the full shrunken-LFC ranking rather than an over-representation test on a thresholded list — with n=3 the significant-gene list may be short or empty, and a ranking-based test still returns interpretable signal in that case. Liver plus 'drug treatment' makes xenobiotic metabolism, oxidative stress and bile-acid response the pathways to report explicitly whether or not they clear significance. T4S1 synthesises: the gene table, the two-method concordance, the power audit, and an explicit statement of what this design cannot support.

No drug identity, dose, exposure, or outcome data is present, so no PK/PD, safety, or repurposing step is planned — those would be speculation on this input.

Section 4: the confidence answer from T2S1 — observed BCV, minimum detectable fold change at 80% power, the fraction of the transcriptome effectively untestable at this n, and the permutation comparison with its 1/10 resolution floor stated. Section 5: pathway-level context from T3S1, labelled as coordinated expression shift and not mechanism. Section 6: explicit limitations — what this design cannot establish (no dose, no time course, no drug identity in the profiled metadata, no paired structure, no independent replication cohort), and a concrete recommendation for the replicate count that would be needed to detect the fold-change range actually observed here. Produce a ranked shortlist of candidate genes for orthogonal validation (qPCR or an independent cohort), ordered by cross-method agreement and effect size rather than by p-value alone.
steps.context: This is the deliverable that answers both halves of the research question in one place. It must not upgrade the certainty of any upstream step. If the analysis found few or no genes, the report says that and quantifies why, which is a complete and useful answer.
acceptance_criteria: The report states the number of high-confidence genes (all three methods) explicitly, including zero if that is the result
Effect sizes with standard errors accompany every gene called out by name
The confidence section gives numbers (BCV, minimum detectable fold change, untestable fraction) rather than adjectives
A replicate-count recommendation grounded in the observed dispersion is given
Limitations section names the absence of dose, time-course, drug identity and validation cohort
constraints: Do not describe any gene as a biomarker, target, or mechanism — no such evidence exists in this dataset

Do not present nominal p-values as the primary result if padj-significant genes are few; if nominal results are shown, label them as hypothesis-generating and give the expected false-positive count at that threshold
Every quantitative claim must trace to an upstream step's output
Use the actual condition labels from metadata.csv throughout
caveats: The temptation at n=3 is to loosen thresholds until a story appears; the report must resist this and state the underpowered case plainly if that is what the data show
Cross-method agreement reduces method-specific artefacts but does not protect against a shared confounder such as an unrecorded batch or a single outlier sample driving the contrast
